newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-GOUGH STAKES NEW-BALL CLAIM WITH FIVE-WICKET HAUL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH STAKES NEW-BALL CLAIM WITH FIVE-WICKET HAUL.

text.p: Darren Gough staked his claim to open England's attack in next week's first test against Zimbabwe with a five-wicket haul against Matabeleland on Wednesday.
Gough's five for 62 put England in command as Matabeleland were reduced to 181 for nine on the second day of their four-day game in reply to the touring team's 334.
Gough bowled three fiery spells and took wickets each time. Phil Tufnell and Andy Caddick shared the other four wickets.
The only Matabeleland batsman to prosper was wicketkeeper Wayne James but he needed plenty of luck to score 62 before falling caught and bowled to Tufnell. He hit 11 boundaries in his 113-ball stay.
Earlier, England's batsmen squandered the previous day's good work, adding just 135 runs for their last seven wickets.

Resuming at 199 for three, England were dismissed shortly after lunch for 334. Nick Knight, 100 not out overnight, added just 14 before he was caught at second slip off John Rennie. His 208-ball innings included 16 fours.
John Crawley hit nine boundaries before he was caught by James off Heath Streak for 63.
